subject.title: Feature: Activity-based heartbeat with idle timeout

question: What heartbeat idle policy should OpenClaw support: a new explicit idle-timeout config, reuse existing session freshness, or a broader heartbeat cost/backoff policy?
rationale: This adds public heartbeat configuration and changes scheduled background behavior, so automation cannot safely choose the config contract, defaults, bypass rules, and upgrade semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve explicit idle-timeout config
options.body: Add a heartbeat-owned idle timeout option with documented activity semantics and tests for scheduled runs versus wake/event bypasses.

options.title: Reuse session freshness only
options.body: Gate scheduled heartbeat on existing session reset freshness without adding a new heartbeat config key, reducing surface but giving users less direct control.

options.title: Fold into broader heartbeat safety policy
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers design combined idle, cost-cap, OK-backoff, and provider-error backoff semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve explicit idle-timeout config
recommendation.body: Add a heartbeat-owned idle timeout option with documented activity semantics and tests for scheduled runs versus wake/event bypasses.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent history across heartbeat runner, config/docs work, and prior tracker review.
